[https://d15k2d11r6t6rl.cloudfront.net/public/users/Integrators/04eaa6b2-88f4-43b4-b978-7bb0708f5838/7237344C447445787878394747342B75584E47375A57552F745265427662334B544A4A36505A58657A5871474B7A5A6E53705571424758325657365969365747/editor_images/WCM%20logo.JPG] #CourtsMatter
This past Friday, Courts delivered wins for Pennsylvania voters [https://www.democracydocket.com/news-alerts/a-double-win-for-voters-in-pennsylvania] . One ruling ensured that undated or wrongly dated mail-in ballots will be counted, while the other rejected a bid to purge more than 277,000 from the state’s voter rolls.
First, the 3rd U.S. Circuit Court of Appeals denied [https://www.democracydocket.com/wp-content/uploads/2022/11/445-2025-04-24-Order-denying-PA-Attorney-Generals-motion-to-intervene.pdf] a request by Pennsylvania Attorney General Dave Sunday (R), on behalf of the state, to halt a recent federal court ruling that Pennsylvania must count undated or wrongly dated mail-in ballots.
The ruling stemmed from a lawsuit originally filed [https://www.democracydocket.com/cases/pennsylvania-undated-and-wrongly-dated-mail-in-ballots-challenge-eakin/] in 2022, challenging the state’s instructions to county boards of elections that any mail-in ballot that’s timely cast but either missing a date or containing the wrong date on the outer return envelopes should not be counted.
After the federal judge’s ruling in March of this year, the plaintiffs appealed [https://www.democracydocket.com/wp-content/uploads/2022/11/441-2025-04-02-Notice-Of-Appeal-.pdf] the decision to the 3rd Circuit. The appeal remains ongoing, but today’s order ensures that counties will count wrongly dated and undated ballots during this month’s primary.
Second, a Pennsylvania district court judge dismissed a lawsuit by the 1789 Foundation to have hundreds of thousands of voters purged from Pennsylvania’s voter rolls.The 1789 Foundation, also known as Citizen_AG, filed [https://www.democracydocket.com/wp-content/uploads/2024/10/1-2024-10-29-Complaint.pdf] a lawsuit in October against Pennsylvania Secretary of State Al Schmidt (R) claiming Schmidt failed to maintain voter rolls in line with the National Voter Registration Act.
The group wanted the court to force Pennsylvania to remove 277,000 registrants who did not respond to confirmation notices in the 2020 general election cycle removed from the voter rolls.
District Court judge Robert Mariani dismissed [https://www.democracydocket.com/wp-content/uploads/2024/10/67-2025-05-02-Memorandum-.pdf] the 1789 Foundation’s lawsuit on the grounds that the organization lacked standing to bring the case in the first place.
In law, standing [https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Standing_(law)] is a condition that a party seeking a legal remedy must show they have, by demonstrating to the court, sufficient connection to and harm from the law or action challenged to support the party's participation in the case.
In other news, this year marks the 15th anniversary of a landmark U.S. Supreme Court ruling that fundamentally reshaped the world of campaign finance. For good-government supporters, it’s a somber milestone. Find out why in Spotlight PA’s full report. [https://www.spotlightpa.org/news/2025/05/citizens-united-supreme-court-ruling-campaign-finance-dark-money]
The 2010 decision in Citizens United v. Federal Election Commission , they say, vastly expanded the role of big money in politics and ushered in an era of unprecedented — and in some cases, untraceable — spending on elections by ultra-wealthy special interests.
In Pennsylvania, the court decision’s impact on races for state and local offices was muted — at least early on. That is because of Pennsylvania’s notoriously lax campaign finance laws. Some state lawmakers have sought to tighten rules around so-called “dark money” groups, but their legislation didn’t make it through the full legislature. Continue reading for more on Citizens United and its lasting impact [https://www.spotlightpa.org/news/2025/05/citizens-united-supreme-court-ruling-campaign-finance-dark-money] .
[https://prod.cdn.everyaction.com/images/van/EA/EA016/1/99735/images/DelCo_2.png] We are hiring!
Let's provide civic education together!
We're looking for people passionate about voting rights in Philadelphia, Allegheny, Erie, Lawrence, Bucks, Montgomery, Chester, and Delaware County to help us shape the future of Pennsylvania.
Join our team and help us provide civic education in our communities and register folks to vote!
Positions start at $20 an hour.
Interested? Contact jobs@nppef.org [jobs@nppef.org]
EMAIL US [jobs@nppef.org]
News You Can Use
There are things every one of us can do [https://www.democracydocket.com/opinion/we-have-more-power-than-trump-wants-us-to-believe-heres-what-you-can-do/] in our daily lives to help ensure free and fair elections. Some actions are small — so small that you might dismiss them as unimportant. Don’t. Every important journey begins with a single step, and the first is no less important than the last.
1. Educate Yourself
Elections can be complicated. The rules vary from state to state — and sometimes even from county to county. These rules also change frequently due to new laws, policies or court rulings. My first recommendation: spend time each month learning what’s happening with voting laws in your state and nationally.
Spotlight PA has an 2025 Election Center [https://www.spotlightpa.org/elections] with all the information you need to be prepared to vote this year, including guides to the big races, key dates, and more.
* New: Which Pittsburgh mayoral candidate most aligns with you? Take our quiz [https://www.spotlightpa.org/news/2025/05/pittsburgh-mayor-election-2025-candidates-quiz]
* Get answers to your questions with our AI-powered Election Assistant [https://www.spotlightpa.org/elections/assistant/]
* Everything you need to know about mail voting [https://www.spotlightpa.org/news/2025/04/pennsylvania-primary-election-2025-mail-ballot-how-to-request-fill-out-return] , becoming a poll worker [https://www.spotlightpa.org/news/2025/04/pennsylvania-primary-election-2025-how-to-be-poll-worker-guide]
* Everything you need to know about how to vote and where to vote [https://www.spotlightpa.org/news/2025/05/pennsylvania-primary-election-day-2025-voter-information-registration]
* Guides to Commonwealth, Superior Courts [https://www.spotlightpa.org/news/2025/04/pennsylvania-primary-election-2025-commonwealth-superior-court-candidates] , vetting judicial candidates [https://www.spotlightpa.org/news/2025/04/pennsylvania-primary-election-2025-candidate-vetting-guide]
* Guides to State College school board [https://www.spotlightpa.org/statecollege/2025/04/pennsylvania-primary-election-2025-state-college-school-board-anderson-huff-barlow-black-desmarais-mcternan-sogor] , Reading City Council president [https://www.spotlightpa.org/berks/2025/04/reading-city-council-president-primary-election-2025]
* Guides to voting as a college student [https://www.spotlightpa.org/news/2025/04/pennsylvania-primary-election-2025-college-student-voting-guide]
En Español
* Guía para votar por correo [https://www.spotlightpa.org/news/2025/04/pensilvania-elecciones-primarias-2025-votar-correo-como-llenar] , la presidencia del Concejo Municipal de Reading [https://www.spotlightpa.org/news/2025/04/reading-concejo-municipal-primarias-elecciones-2025]
* Guía para quién está en la papeleta de las primarias [https://www.spotlightpa.org/news/2025/05/pensilvania-primarias-elecciones-2025-votar-informacion] , cómo convertirse en trabajador electoral el 20 de mayo [https://www.spotlightpa.org/news/2025/05/pensilvania-elecciones-2025-como-convertirse-trabajador-electoral]
2. Stay Engaged
To protect democracy, we all must stay engaged day in and day out. We can’t just show up right before an election and tune out afterward. If we remain committed, democracy will win.
Check out a Montgomery County Commissioner’s effort to educate voters. It's now an emmy-nominated short film. “Running elections in Pennsylvania's third-most-populous county, Neil Makhija said he’s seen the slippery slope from election misinformation to political violence.” ( Philadelphia Inquirer [https://www.inquirer.com/politics/pennsylvania/montgomery-county-commissioner-neil-makhija-emmy-20250508.html] )
3. Share What You Learn
Once you’ve figured out what’s going on, share that information with your networks and community. It might feel awkward to bring up voter suppression or changes in election laws when we’re not in the middle of a major election — but local elections happen in off years, and special elections are more common than you think. Now is the perfect time to start conversations about voting.
Here, in Pennsylvania, we vote every year, twice a year!
4. Join or Support Pro-Democracy Organizations
Is partisan politics not for you? There are numerous nonprofits and grassroots organizations working every day to protect voting rights and ensure free and fair elections. Supporting these groups with your time or resources helps these groups do their work.
Check out the work New PA Project has been up to lately below. AND , check out our upcoming events listed above!
5. Become a Trained Poll Worker
Many counties face a shortage of poll workers, especially during election season. Being a poll worker requires dedication, attention to detail and a willingness to be trained. It’s a meaningful way to serve your community and help protect the integrity of the voting process.

Call and write your elected officials at the federal, state and local levels. Tell them that protecting voting rights and ensuring free and fair elections are your top priorities. Even better, show up at public meetings. Ask them directly what they’re doing to combat voter suppression. Be informed about pending legislation and urge them to support pro-democracy initiatives. This applies no matter where you live or who represents you — Democrat or Republican. Constituent pressure always matters. Don’t let anyone tell you otherwise.

Yes — every election. That means local elections, primary elections and special elections. Become a super-voter. The more you vote, the more informed and engaged you become. You’ll also be better positioned to notice and report problems — like changes to polling locations or voting equipment — that could impact turnout or accessibility.
Make a plan to vote in the primary election, Tuesday, May 20th. When are you voting this year? Who are you going with? How are you voting this year -- by mail or on Election Day? As a reminder, the last day to request a mail ballot is Tuesday, May 13th!

clean_body: [] Hi Friend, Welcome to the latest New PA Project Education Fund (NPPEF) newsletter! Earlier this week, the PA [] House State Government Committee [] [] voted on two bills that have the potential to impact our voting rights: State Rep Mehaffie's Voter ID bill (HB771) and State Rep. McClinton's omnibus bill (HB1396). Both passed out of committee this week and will now be voted on by the full house. An omnibus bill is a legislative bill that combines multiple, sometimes unrelated, provisions or bills into one single bill. It's essentially a package deal of different legislative proposals, often used to facilitate the passage of legislation, particularly appropriations bills. HB 771 is sponsored by State Rep. Thomas Mehaffie (Dauphin) and “would require all voters arriving at their election precincts to show identification or attest under penalty of law that they are legally able to vote in Pennsylvania.” State Rep. Malcolm Kenyatta (Philadelphia) voiced his opposition to the bill. The bill doesn’t address [] the real issues at stake. “We need to solve problems of voter irregularities and voter fraud,” he said. “We do not have demonstrable evidence that leads us to make the point that we need to address voter ID in this way. Let’s talk about the issues that do exist. This legislation doesn’t address those.” HB 1396 has a more recognizable name behind it – Speaker of the State House Joanna McClinton (Delaware/Philadelphia). State Rep. Ben Waxman (Philadelphia) complemented the Speaker, saying that the legislation is a “comprehensive approach to election reform that tries to dramatically improve the process and makes administration of elections much smoother.” Among other changes, [] House Bill 1396 would also give election workers up to a week before Election Day to prepare to count mail-in ballots, a process that has been a bottleneck for election results in parts of the state, providing fodder for election deniers. The vote-by-mail provision has been the subject of numerous lawsuits, including one now before the U.S. Supreme Court, as candidates and parties have argued over how election officials should handle irregularities, such as errors on completed ballots, that are not explicitly addressed. The bill would make clear that county election officials are required to notify voters if their mail-in ballots have been rejected for the lack of a signature and give the voter an opportunity to “cure” the error. She co-founded Young Professionals of Color–Greater Harrisburg (YPOC), an organization dedicated to fostering leadership, advocacy, and professional growth for communities of color. Request a mail-in ballot or find your local ballot drop-off location here [vote.pa] Your county election office must receive your completed mail ballot by 8PM on May 20th. We recommend mailing it at least 5 days prior, or delivering it by hand at an official ballot drop off location. #GoVotePA SHARE ON INSTAGRAM [] [] #CourtsMatter This past Friday, Courts delivered wins for Pennsylvania voters [] . One ruling ensured that undated or wrongly dated mail-in ballots will be counted, while the other rejected a bid to purge more than 277,000 from the state’s voter rolls. First, the 3rd U.S. Circuit Court of Appeals denied [] a request by Pennsylvania Attorney General Dave Sunday (R), on behalf of the state, to halt a recent federal court ruling that Pennsylvania must count undated or wrongly dated mail-in ballots. The ruling stemmed from a lawsuit originally filed [] in 2022, challenging the state’s instructions to county boards of elections that any mail-in ballot that’s timely cast but either missing a date or containing the wrong date on the outer return envelopes should not be counted. After the federal judge’s ruling in March of this year, the plaintiffs appealed [] the decision to the 3rd Circuit. The appeal remains ongoing, but today’s order ensures that counties will count wrongly dated and undated ballots during this month’s primary. Second, a Pennsylvania district court judge dismissed a lawsuit by the 1789 Foundation to have hundreds of thousands of voters purged from Pennsylvania’s voter rolls.The 1789 Foundation, also known as CitizenAG, filed [] a lawsuit in October against Pennsylvania Secretary of State Al Schmidt (R) claiming Schmidt failed to maintain voter rolls in line with the National Voter Registration Act. The group wanted the court to force Pennsylvania to remove 277,000 registrants who did not respond to confirmation notices in the 2020 general election cycle removed from the voter rolls. District Court judge Robert Mariani dismissed [] the 1789 Foundation’s lawsuit on the grounds that the organization lacked standing to bring the case in the first place. In law, standing [)] is a condition that a party seeking a legal remedy must show they have, by demonstrating to the court, sufficient connection to and harm from the law or action challenged to support the party's participation in the case. Today’s the day!

I’m up bright and early to submit my ballot and make my voice heard in
today’s election, and I hope today you’ll do the
same.

Polls are open all over Michigan — and if you take nothing else from this
message, I hope you’ll take the time to make your voice heard today! [ https://act.jocelynbenson.com/go/25180?t=1001&akid=2139%2E181023%2E6L4hp8 ]If
you need any assistance finding your polling location, click here for more
information →

[ https://act.jocelynbenson.com/go/25180?t=1002&akid=2139%2E181023%2E6L4hp8 ]Find Your Polling Location

coworkers to remind them to get their ballots in today!

I’ll be making one last trip on the campaign trail today to rally our
supporters, turn out the vote, and share my vision for Michigan with the
final few undecided voters who could very well determine the outcome of
this race.

In other words, I’m leaving everything I possibly have out on the trail
today. When the polls close tonight at 8 p.m., I want to know I did
everything in my power to make our plan for Michigan a reality — and if

_**Patriot**_ , I’m going to keep this short, because it comes from the heart and those kind of things don’t need a lot of words. **In just hours, the votes will be cas t.** I’ve been sitting here thinking about the miles we’ve put behind us to get to this point, and more than anything, thinking about you, **Patriot**. You know, back home in Jackson, we’ve got a saying: You find out who’s really in your corner when the road gets tough. _**Patriot**_ , you’ve been in my corner every single mile of this haul. body:

---
| |
# Conforti Grassroots Newsletter
---
| | | | | | | | | | |
---
| | | | | | | | | | | |

**A Message From Niki Conforti:**.Today is the day, and the future of Illinois’ 6th Congressional District is officially in your hands. As we reach the finish line on this November 3rd Election Day, I am urging every single resident who has not yet cast a ballot to head to the polls today and make your voice heard. For far too long, hardworking families in Cook and DuPage counties have been forced to deplete their savings just to get by under the failed, tax-and-spend policies of incumbent Sean Casten. We cannot afford another term of partisan messaging and appeasing special interests while our utility bills, grocery costs, and taxes skyrocket. If you haven’t already voted early or by mail, please take the time today to go to your local polling place, bring your friends and neighbors, and vote for sensible, common-sense leadership that puts our community first..From the bottom of my heart, thank you for the incredible support, energy, and grassroots momentum you have poured into this campaign from day one. Whether you displayed a yard sign on your lawn, walked alongside our team in summer parades, or simply took a moment to talk at your doorstep, your dedication has been the driving force behind everything we have built. Having lived in the 6th District for the majority of my life, I have always known how resilient and hardworking our neighborhoods are, and standing shoulder-to-shoulder with you throughout this race has been the honor of a lifetime..With your support, I am ready to take a strict "district-first" mentality to Washington, D.C., and immediately get to work bending the cost curve for Illinois families. Drawing on my professional background as an energy consultant and a former healthcare executive for twelve years, I will fight to cut burdensome energy regulations in favor of "speed to power" to lower your utility bills, and enforce strict medical billing transparency to foster competition and drive down healthcare costs. Furthermore, I will push for statutory federal spending caps to rein in the runaway national debt and stop tax hikes, incentivize the return of manufacturing and good-paying jobs to the 6th District, secure our southern border while fully backing our local police, and fiercely protect parental rights and fair play for female athletes under Title IX. Together, we will restore accountability to Congress—and after the polls close tonight, I hope to see you at our Official Election Night Watch Party at Salerno’s Pizzeria & Sports Bar in Hodgkins at 6:30 PM as we celebrate our shared vision for the 6th District!
---
| |
---
| |
### District-First Movement.
---
| |
---
| | | | | | | | | | |
---
| | |
## Celebrating America’s 250th Birthday Across the District

## (May – July 2026)

---
| |
Walking alongside hundreds of supporters, veterans, and families during our local summer parades was an unforgettable highlight of this cycle. From kicking off the season at the 108th Elmhurst Memorial Day Parade and gathering at the Veterans Memorial in Wilder Park, to celebrating the 250th anniversary of the United States at the Garfield Ridge, Oak Lawn, Villa Park ("Stars, Stripes, and 250 Lights"), and Downers Grove Independence Day parades, the patriotic spirit and warmth of our communities were on full display.
---
|
---
| | | | | | | | | | |
---
| | |
# Grassroots Conversations Over Coffee
---
| | **(June – August 2026)**
---
| | Some of the most meaningful moments of the campaign happened face-to-face with neighbors discussing real kitchen-table issues. Grabbing one-on-one conversations during "Coffee with Niki" at Krema Coffee in Tinley Park, and diving into solutions for skyrocketing utility bills at the Elmhurst American Legion energy forum reminded us daily why our "district-first" mission matters so much.
---
|
---
| | | | | | | | | | |
---
| | |
# Momentum in Lombard & Autumn in Palos Park
---
| | **(August – September 2026)**
---
| |

As the campaign shifted into high gear, the energy at our August reception in Lombard with special guest Congressman Darin LaHood showed just how united Illinoisans are in fighting for fiscal responsibility. Shortly after, marching down 123rd Street with our dedicated volunteers at the Palos Park Autumn In The Park Festival Parade and meeting voters at the Oak Lawn VFW with the Worth Township Republican Organization gave our team the exact surge of momentum needed to carry us through to Election Day.

| | | | JoCasta Zamarripa is a lifelong Milwaukeean, a proud daughter of the city’s south side, and a dedicated public servant who’s never stopped fighting for working people. Born and raised in the very neighborhoods she now represents, JoCasta has spent her life pushing for progress that reflects the realities of everyday Wisconsinites.

[ ](https://us.list-manage.com/JQzsOBT7jZV?e=8d919f2092&c2id=0bdcb6d83cbc8b2aaf05afb952b88bb7)

She made history as the first Latina and first openly bi member of both the Wisconsin State Legislature and the Milwaukee Common Council. But JoCasta’s leadership is defined by more than her historic firsts—it's grounded in results. She served ten years in the State Assembly and is now in her second term as Alderperson for Milwaukee’s 8th District, where she’s led major efforts on affordable housing, small business licensing reform, and community development.

In 2025, she was the lead sponsor of the Housing Element Plan, a key step in addressing Milwaukee’s housing crisis by expanding affordable options and preventing displacement. Her approach is practical and persistent—building coalitions, navigating political challenges, and staying rooted in the neighborhoods she serves.

Now, JoCasta is running as a Democrat for Wisconsin Secretary of State to use the platform to fight for what matters: more funding for our schools so families aren’t forced into referenda every election, real housing relief for working people, and affordable child care that lets parents breathe.

body:
Don’t hesitate to send one last voting reminder
| [](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/142795154/658095891/-3547583?nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9FQS9FQTAxMy8xLzg5Mjk0IiwNCiAgIkRpc3RyaWJ1dGlvblVuaXF1ZUlkIjogIjViOTcxZjdhLTg2ZDctZjExMS1iZjViLTAwMGQzYTU0NDQyZSIsDQogICJFbWFpbEFkZHJlc3MiOiAiZHB3aWxsaXM2N0BnbWFpbC5jb20iDQp9&hmac=Af_TxMqtrvo-3NUyeC1BdeKrVI5ClelFjJoZJ3cEu_o=&emci=286756fd-ccd6-f111-bf5b-000d3a54442e&emdi=5b971f7a-86d7-f111-bf5b-000d3a54442e&ceid=8431045)
---

Peter, do you know someone who hasn’t voted yet? Do you know someone who _maaaaaaybe_ hasn’t voted yet? If so, don’t hesitate. Don’t worry about whether you’re pestering them. Give them the nudge they need to get off their keisters and get to the polls. **Send them this link so they can find out where to vote and make a plan before polls close:[iwillvote.com](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/142795156/658095893/-1612268846?nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9FQS9FQTAxMy8xLzg5Mjk0IiwNCiAgIkRpc3RyaWJ1dGlvblVuaXF1ZUlkIjogIjViOTcxZjdhLTg2ZDctZjExMS1iZjViLTAwMGQzYTU0NDQyZSIsDQogICJFbWFpbEFkZHJlc3MiOiAiZHB3aWxsaXM2N0BnbWFpbC5jb20iDQp9&hmac=Af_TxMqtrvo-3NUyeC1BdeKrVI5ClelFjJoZJ3cEu_o=&emci=286756fd-ccd6-f111-bf5b-000d3a54442e&emdi=5b971f7a-86d7-f111-bf5b-000d3a54442e&ceid=8431045)** Even if they don’t thank you, we will. Our democracy will too. Once that’s done, if you’ve still got a case of the Election Day jitters, consider putting your money where your anxiety is. [**Invest in our fight for democracy, because our work doesn’t end when the polls close. (In fact, it’s bound to get even more urgent.)**](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/142795157/658095896/1548394306?refcode=don_ndrc_tier1_email_HasntVotedYet_email_20261103-NDRC-Tier1-HasntVotedYet_&utm_source=email&utm_medium=email&utm_term=don&utm_content=20261103-NDRC-Tier1-HasntVotedYet_&utm_campaign=HasntVotedYet&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9FQS9FQTAxMy8xLzg5Mjk0IiwNCiAgIkRpc3RyaWJ1dGlvblVuaXF1ZUlkIjogIjViOTcxZjdhLTg2ZDctZjExMS1iZjViLTAwMGQzYTU0NDQyZSIsDQogICJFbWFpbEFkZHJlc3MiOiAiZHB3aWxsaXM2N0BnbWFpbC5jb20iDQp9&hmac=Af_TxMqtrvo-3NUyeC1BdeKrVI5ClelFjJoZJ3cEu_o=) It’s easy to imagine the worst-case scenarios and the shady tactics Republicans could engage in for the next few days and weeks. |
---
******TFVC Legislative Director Emily Cameron** joined a packed crowd in Parker County for **Vice President JD Vance’s GOTV rally**. Vance emphasized Texas’s importance on the national political stage and stated that "Texas is NOT becoming California!" **His charge to voters:**
**“I need you to send a message on Nov. 3 that America belongs to the people who love it, not those who hate it.”**

**TFVC OP Whitney** is bringing medical liberty directly to her community in Beaumont. A final message from Brad Smith. Thank you for everything you've done. Today, let's finish what we started.

| | | | | | | [View this email in your browser](https://mailchi.mp/0be7f1601f8c/officially-on-the-ballot-and-building-momentum-every-day-17461981?e=a4a0e00aa9)

Hi Peter,

Today is Election Day, and polls are now open!
When I started this campaign, I never imagined the incredible support, dedication, and energy we would build together. Every door knocked, every dollar donated, and every conversation has brought us to this moment. I am deeply grateful to everyone who has been part of this journey.
---
| | | | | | | | | | [|
---](https://us.list-manage.com/ZxyBqLocBoK?e=a4a0e00aa9&c2id=92e2d37cfd6b9cebafd3106e51945da8)
| | Now, after months of hard work, it all comes down to one powerful action. **VOTE.**
**We can't expect change if we don't make one.**
If you live in Wisconsin's 6th Congressional District, I'm asking for your vote today, November 3. Make a plan, find your polling location, and make your voice heard.
**Find your polling location:**
[https://myvote.wi.gov/en-us/Find-My-Polling-Place](https://us.list-manage.com/1C_7tXT82KB?e=a4a0e00aa9&c2id=92e2d37cfd6b9cebafd3106e51945da8)
Polls are open until **8:00 p.m.** , and our work isn't finished until they close.
No matter the outcome, I am incredibly proud of what we've built together. Thank you for believing in this campaign, standing alongside me, and showing what's possible when we come together for our communities.
**Let's finish what we started.**

| | **_Meet Russell:_** Born and raised in Surfside Beach, SC, Congressman Russell Fry is the proud and homegrown Representative for South Carolina’s 7th Congressional District. Growing up in a cinder block home with no heating or air conditioning, Russell learned at an early age that hard work and perseverance pave the only true path to the American Dream. He watched his parents work day in and day out to make ends meet. And the values they instilled in him during his upbringing led Russell to self-fund both his undergraduate education at the University of South Carolina, and later his law studies at the Charleston School of Law. At Charleston, Russell served as the President of the Student Bar Association and even helped the school achieve its American Bar Association accreditation. He went on to practice law in the Grand Strand area for over a decade before entering the political arena to serve in the South Carolina House of Representatives for State House District 106 (Horry County). During his seven-year tenure in the SC House, Russell fought to safeguard Constitutional liberties, lower taxes, and put the best interests of South Carolina families above all else. He climbed the ranks to become Chief Majority Whip, and also chaired the House Opioid Prevention Study Committee. Under Russell’s leadership, 18 policy initiatives to combat the opioid crisis were signed into law. Since the first day he stepped foot in Washington, Russell has strived to shake up the corrupt status quo and deliver real change for the American people. He believes adamantly that so long as the American people stand united, we can keep the American Dream alive for every citizen of our great nation. Russell is a dedicated husband to his wife, Bronwen, and a loving father to his son, James. The family lives in Murrells Inlet with their chocolate lab, Jasper.

From 7:00 this morning until 7:00 tonight, South Carolina can walk in and vote for who represents us. If you are in line at 7 PM, you can still cast a ballot. After that, it is over. Russell Fry Trump Endorsed U.S. Congressman SC-07 | | | == | | | Meet Russell: Born and raised in Surfside Beach, SC, Congressman Russell Fry is the proud and homegrown Representative for South Carolina’s 7th Congressional District. Growing up in a cinder block home with no heating or air conditioning, Russell learned at an early age that hard work and perseverance pave the only true path to the American Dream. He watched his parents work day in and day out to make ends meet. And the values they instilled in him during his upbringing led Russell to self-fund both his undergraduate education at the University of South Carolina, and later his law studies at the Charleston School of Law. At Charleston, Russell served as the President of the Student Bar Association and even helped the school achieve its American Bar Association accreditation. He went on to practice law in the Grand Strand area for over a decade before entering the political arena to serve in the South Carolina House of Representatives for State House District 106 (Horry County). During his seven-year tenure in the SC House, Russell fought to safeguard Constitutional liberties, lower taxes, and put the best interests of South Carolina families above all else. He climbed the ranks to become Chief Majority Whip, and also chaired the House Opioid Prevention Study Committee. Under Russell’s leadership, 18 policy initiatives to combat the opioid crisis were signed into law. Since the first day he stepped foot in Washington, Russell has strived to shake up the corrupt status quo and deliver real change for the American people. He believes adamantly that so long as the American people stand united, we can keep the American Dream alive for every citizen of our great nation. Russell is a dedicated husband to his wife, Bronwen, and a loving father to his son, James. Peter,
**Today is the day we beat Greg Abbott.**
It’s Election Day, and Texans are heading to the polls right now to cast their votes.
The polls show this race is still neck-and-neck, and we have a real opportunity to end Greg Abbott’s era of corruption and bring about the change Texans crave.
We started this campaign with a simple message I learned from my grandmother.
_No te dejes._
Don’t let them push you around. Fight back.

Everything we’ve been working for has led to this very moment. And now I’m asking for your support again to power this campaign through its final day.

Let's bring it home.

Hey everybody, I wanted to share this video with you now that polls are open here in Ohio.
To Martin Sheen, thanks for helping us pull it off.
To you, thanks for believing in me and our message for Ohio, and fighting for it until the end.
-Sherrod
[](https://substack.com/redirect/9a5d0b34-541d-4f40-bc58-aa0c7c3f19cb?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
> _It 's always been Ohio against the world._
> _This Election Day, that 's never been more true._
> _Ohioans are tough, and when people count us out, we always prove them wrong._
> _From pioneers of the skies to travelers of the stars, Ohio is the birthplace of dreamers and doers - those devoted to something bigger than themselves._
> _We work hard, and when we 've given all we can, we push a little more._
> _We know nothing worth having is given. It must be earned._
> _But billionaires consumed by greed and corruption take and take and take, thinking we won 't fight back._
> _So you see, it still is Ohio against the world._
> _We 're standing up to billionaires and corporations, instead of standing with them._
> _We 're demanding a leader who takes on corruption._
> _And when the votes are counted, the message will be clear:_
> _When Ohio shows up to fight, we never back down._
* * *
Before you click away!
Our resources are zeroed out. We've allocated every dollar that came in the door to reach voters before polls close tonight. That means our accounts will be empty (or maybe even a little in the red). That's on purpose. **But it 's also taking a big risk.**
If the result is too close to call and Sherrod's fight continues beyond tonight, we won't have the resources we need to wage it. Outside groups have shown they're willing to spend ungodly sums to buy this seat. We can only expect they'll do the same with Senate control still on the line.

Keep reading for answers to some of the most common questions voters have! 👇
* * *
**Where do I go to drop off a ballot, or vote in person?**
Enter the residential address where you are registered to vote into the Colorado Secretary of State’s website to find where to drop off your ballot or go vote in person! | | [FIND YOUR POLLING PLACE](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/142803498/658106144/128464908?refcode=ea.b11164df-8ed7-f111-bf5b-000d3a54442e&ms=ea.b11164df-8ed7-f111-bf5b-000d3a54442e&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQMTAvMS84MTM2MiIsDQogICJEaXN0cmlidXRpb25VbmlxdWVJZCI6ICJiMTExNjRkZi04ZWQ3LWYxMTEtYmY1Yi0wMDBkM2E1NDQ0MmUiLA0KICAiRW1haWxBZGRyZXNzIjogImRwd2lsbGlzNjdAZ21haWwuY29tIg0KfQ%3D%3D&hmac=6AZIjTpxMs2OtkCOIcWwt-Ht3OEytdSqaTXq21wO-Ic=&emci=0a5e307e-fad6-f111-bf5b-000d3a54442e&emdi=b11164df-8ed7-f111-bf5b-000d3a54442e&ceid=51844520)
---
* * *
**Can I still mail in my ballot?**
Because today is Election Day, it is too late to mail your ballot. You must drop off your ballot in a secure drop box or vote in person.
* * *
**What if I can’t find what I’m looking for on the website?**
Contact your county clerk for nearby locations and hours where you may be able to vote in person.
| [CONTACT COUNTY CLERK](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/142803501/658106148/-723356828?refcode=ea.b11164df-8ed7-f111-bf5b-000d3a54442e&ms=ea.b11164df-8ed7-f111-bf5b-000d3a54442e&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQMTAvMS84MTM2MiIsDQogICJEaXN0cmlidXRpb25VbmlxdWVJZCI6ICJiMTExNjRkZi04ZWQ3LWYxMTEtYmY1Yi0wMDBkM2E1NDQ0MmUiLA0KICAiRW1haWxBZGRyZXNzIjogImRwd2lsbGlzNjdAZ21haWwuY29tIg0KfQ%3D%3D&hmac=6AZIjTpxMs2OtkCOIcWwt-Ht3OEytdSqaTXq21wO-Ic=&emci=0a5e307e-fad6-f111-bf5b-000d3a54442e&emdi=b11164df-8ed7-f111-bf5b-000d3a54442e&ceid=51844520)
---
* * *
**How can I check on the status of my ballot if I’ve already mailed it in?**
Check your ballot’s status right here!
| [CHECK ON YOUR BALLOT](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/142803503/658106150/-382893027?refcode=ea.b11164df-8ed7-f111-bf5b-000d3a54442e&ms=ea.b11164df-8ed7-f111-bf5b-000d3a54442e&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQMTAvMS84MTM2MiIsDQogICJEaXN0cmlidXRpb25VbmlxdWVJZCI6ICJiMTExNjRkZi04ZWQ3LWYxMTEtYmY1Yi0wMDBkM2E1NDQ0MmUiLA0KICAiRW1haWxBZGRyZXNzIjogImRwd2lsbGlzNjdAZ21haWwuY29tIg0KfQ%3D%3D&hmac=6AZIjTpxMs2OtkCOIcWwt-Ht3OEytdSqaTXq21wO-Ic=&emci=0a5e307e-fad6-f111-bf5b-000d3a54442e&emdi=b11164df-8ed7-f111-bf5b-000d3a54442e&ceid=51844520)
---
* * *
**I think someone might be trying to interfere with my right to vote... what should I do?**
If you’re at the polls and think you may be experiencing intimidation, it could be illegal — and you have rights. Call the Election Protection Hotline number right away: **1-866-OUR-VOTE** in English, or **1-888-VE-Y-VOTA** en español. _(Pssst: save these numbers now so they’re easy to find later!)_
* * *
**What do I do if I’m voting in person and realize I’ve made a mistake on my ballot?**
If you make a mistake on your ballot, don’t worry — ask a poll worker for a new one.
* * *
It’s time to pull together and finish strong. Thanks for being a voter!
– Team Phil

When I launched this campaign over a year ago -- almost no one gave us a chance.
I was a state representative most of Texas had never heard of, going up against a three-term governor with a lot of money in the bank. The early polls had us down 10 points. We got written off by _almost_ everyone.
Now, we've wiped out that entire 10-point deficit, and today we are leading Greg Abbott in multiple polls.
This has become one of the strongest, most competitive campaigns in the whole country.
**And today, we have the opportunity to do what so many people thought was impossible: elect a new governor and chart a better future for Texas.**
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/02a7f50e-fbe6-4065-bb09-8f243190c8a0?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
The outcome of today's election is the culmination of everything we've worked for.
Grassroots supporters like you are the reason we're in this position, and you're the reason we can finish the job and win this race.
Every ad we ran, every text we sent, and every door we knocked to get our message out only matters if we can get people to the polls today.
**So I 'm asking you to do one more thing: Get out and vote if you haven't already. Remind your friends, your family, and your neighbors now is the time for them to make their voices heard. Polls are open until 7 P.M. and you can find your polling location at [IWillVote.com/TX](https://substack.com/redirect/c281ce10-87be-4ed7-b289-9b16bcab9739?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)**.
I'm running to save Texas schools, put money in your pocket, and end the Greg Abbott Corruption Tax that has meant we pay more while we get less.
**And after everything we 've accomplished together, I believe more than ever that a Texas where we can secure the American Dream is within our reach. One where working families come first, our public schools have the resources they need, and our government works for the people it serves.**
This race is ours to win. We're closer than almost anyone thought we'd be. **Now it 's time to turn that hope into votes and show the country what's possible when Texans come together.**
Let's finish this and take Texas back.
Thank you,
Gina
**P.S.[We're still mobilizing voters. If you can, please make a donation of $10 or more right now to help us get one final surge in grassroots support to get out the vote.](https://substack.com/redirect/71f07b82-d306-4d4d-87fa-1d673b6f0d3c?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)**

subject: Today Is Election Day — Make Your Voice Heard (and Join Us Tonight!)

body:
| | | | | |

| | | | [|

| | Hello Peter,

Today is the day! After months of door-knocking, phone calls, conversations, and community gatherings, it all comes down to this: **Tuesday, November 3, is Election Day.** Polls are open from **6:30 a.m. to 7:30 p.m.** , and if you’re in line by 7:30, you have the right to vote.
Thank you to every one of you who has given your time, your donations, and your belief in a better future for Ohio’s 8th District. Now let’s finish strong together.
**⚠️ Important: If You Have an Absentee Ballot, Do Not Mail It Today**
Ohio’s election law has changed, and there is no longer a grace period for mailed ballots. **Your absentee ballot must arrive at your county Board of Elections by 7:30 p.m. tonight to be counted.** A ballot mailed today will almost certainly arrive too late.
If you still have your absentee ballot:
* **Hand-deliver it to your county Board of Elections office** (or its official drop box) **before 7:30 p.m. today.**
* **Do not take it to your polling place.** Absentee ballots must go to the Board of Elections.
* Make sure the ID envelope is completed and signed.
* You can check your ballot status at **VoteOhio.gov**.

Please forward this to friends and family who voted by mail. One forwarded message could save someone’s vote.
**Vote the Entire Democratic Slate — Top to Bottom** Every race on your ballot matters. The people we elect today shape our schools, our roads, our courts, and our economic future. Please vote for the entire Democratic slate. Your ballot will show only the races for your own district.
**🇺🇸 Federal**
* **U.S. Senate:** Sherrod Brown
* **U.S. House, Ohio’s 8th District:** Vanessa Enoch

_If you live outside the 8th District, please support our Democratic congressional nominee in your district, including Greg Landsman (Hamilton County), Kristina Knickerbocker (Butler County), and Don Leonard (Miami County)._
**🏛️ Statewide (all counties)**
* **Governor & Lt. Governor:** Dr. Amy Acton & David Pepper
* **Attorney General:** John Kulewicz
* **Secretary of State:** Allison Russo
* **Auditor:** Annette Blackwell
* **Treasurer:** Seth Walsh
* **Ohio Supreme Court:** Justice Jennifer Brunner and Judge Marilyn Zayas

**Butler County**

**Preble County**
* Ohio Senate (5th District): Jeffrey Harris
* Ohio House (40th District): Timothy Hornbacker

Not sure where to vote? Find your polling location at **VoteOhio.gov** or **IWillVote.com** , and remember to bring a valid Ohio photo ID.
---
|
---
| |
**🎉 You’re Invited: Election Night Watch Party!** Once you’ve voted, come celebrate with us as the results come in!📍 **Pike 2 Bar & Grill**, 10010 Springfield Pike
🕖 **Starts at 7:00 p.m.**
📞 (513) 938-PIKE
👉 **RSVP here:** [https://campaignhq.app/rsvp/electionnightwatchparty](https://us.list-manage.com/DdFCE4YoTMj?e=c6e7dff14c&c2id=d95570268fc9105c688a303b4f3b91b8)
Great food, great drinks, and great people. Let’s come together and support our community! Bring your friends, your family, and your hope. Whatever tonight brings, we built something powerful together: a movement rooted in community, dignity, and opportunity for every family in the 8th District.
**Three Things You Can Do Right Now**
1. **Vote** , if you haven’t already.
2. **Text or call three people** and remind them to vote, especially anyone still holding an absentee ballot.
3. **RSVP** and join us tonight at Pike 2.

Thank you for standing with me and for believing that our district deserves leadership that listens, works hard, and puts people first. Let’s go make history today.
With deep gratitude and hope,
**Dr. Vanessa Enoch**
Democratic Nominee, Ohio’s 8th Congressional District

name: Chris Pappas
subject: We’ve come so far...
body:
[ https://act.chrispappas.org/go/126?t=1001&akid=9949%2E582294%2E-Hm4QV ]Chris Pappas for Senate[ https://act.chrispappas.org/go/126?t=1002&akid=9949%2E582294%2E-Hm4QV ]Chris Pappas for Senate

I wanted to
take a moment to reflect on how far we’ve come.

But if you don’t have time to read a longer message and want to show your
support before the polls close, [ https://act.chrispappas.org/go/181?c0=em_ms_cp_20261103_2.o2o8TH&refcode=em20261103-2&t=1003&akid=9949%2E582294%2E-Hm4QV ]please chip in $5 or any
amount today.

I didn’t enter public service from a family of career politicians. My
roots are right here in Manchester, shaped behind the counter at my
family’s landmark restaurant.

Growing up working there taught me the value of hard work, accountability,
and serving our community. That’s the exact work ethic I wanted to bring
to Washington to fix a system that no longer works for everyday people.

Now in one of the most critical Senate races in the country, I’m ready to
keep being a voice for all Granite Staters.

We’ve come so far building a true grassroots movement across New
Hampshire, but the contrast in this race could not be clearer.

Our campaign is built by working people pitching in what they can when
they can, while John Sununu is backed by Donald Trump, MAGA billionaires,
and corporate PACs.

Sununu has sold out Granite Staters to corporate special interests like
Big Pharma and Wall Street and grew his net worth up to $35 million.
Granite Staters can’t trust him to fight for them as long as he can line
his own pockets.

With just hours left, everything comes down to this final stretch. I need
your help to make sure we have the resources to reach every last voter so
we can protect this open seat and flip the Senate blue in November.

[ https://act.chrispappas.org/go/181?c0=em_ms_cp_20261103_2.o2o8TH&refcode=em20261103-2&t=1004&akid=9949%2E582294%2E-Hm4QV ]If you’re ready to help us cross the finish line, will you pitch in
$5 or whatever you can today?

[ https://act.chrispappas.org/go/181?c0=em_ms_cp_20261103_2.o2o8TH&amount=5&refcode=em20261103-2&t=1023&akid=9949%2E582294%2E-Hm4QV ]Donate $5 »

Thank you,

Chris

You can unsubscribe from this mailing list at any time:
http://act.chrispappas.org/cms/unsubscribe/unsubscribe/?akid=9949%2E582294%2E-Hm4QV

subject: Your Vote Matters. Polls Close at 8 PM.
disclaimer_text: Paid for and authorized by Bennett for Governor · P
body:
It's Election Day in Maine. Polls are open right now and close at 8:00 tonight.

| | |
---
---
---
---
Hi Peter, It's Election Day in Maine. Polls are open right now and close at 8:00 tonight.

Three things you can do before 8:00 p.m.:
1. **Vote.** [Look up your polling place here.](https://www.supportrickbennett.com/r?u=xDM_o8flxF55aheb-ums81BZNLEmacP4ToqJgnLf3XbSX2YMxRlcgLZ36yCbO9q0NommNHmbf9pvScXLbwCjsyk45_duXESIha5JhAFH-WE&e=939e09e235be96b0bea768d960703804&utm_source=bennettforgovernor&utm_medium=email&utm_campaign=election_day&n=1)
2. **Return your absentee ballot.** If it's still at home, don't mail it. Deliver it in person to your town office or polling place by 8:00 p.m.
3. **Bring one more voter with you.** A spouse, a neighbor, a coworker — offer them a ride.

Whatever happens tonight, our campaign has been about getting a government that will deliver results. Making life affordable for Maine people. Lower energy bills. Housing families can afford it. Property tax relief. A state government that answers to Mainers.

Every vote will matter. Please make sure yours is one of them.

Thank you,

Rick
---

subject: Today Is Election Day. Arizona's Future Is in Your Hands.
disclaimer_text: PAID FOR BY VOTE BOLICK
body:
| | | | | [|
---](https://us.list-manage.com/WKCJSmBy5TM?e=a7ab36849c&c2id=b6e4918ecaa4a9e494d38fc9e6fde211)
| | | | | |
Today is Election Day, and the future of our great state is on the ballot.For years, Arizona has been a beacon of opportunity because voters have supported policies that empower families, protect taxpayers, promote educational freedom, and keep government accountable. Together, we have expanded school choice, kept taxes low, strengthened protections for victims of human trafficking, advanced criminal justice reforms, defended consumers, and worked to keep Arizona one of the best places in America to live, work, and raise a family.**But these accomplishments are not guaranteed to continue.** If Democrats gain control of the Arizona Legislature, many of the policies that have helped make Arizona successful will be at risk. There could be renewed efforts to restrict school choice options for families, increase government spending, expand regulations on businesses and job creators, and move our state in a very different direction. Republicans have fought to protect educational freedom, keep taxes low, support law enforcement, strengthen border security, and preserve the principles of limited government that have helped Arizona thrive.This election is about more than one race or one candidate. It is about the direction of our state for years to come. It is about whether Arizona continues to lead with freedom, opportunity, and personal responsibility, or whether we allow government to play a larger role in the decisions best left to families and local communities.**Every vote matters. Every voice matters.** 🗳️ **Where to vote**

Please return your early ballot to a polling location or ballot drop box before 7pm on November 3rd. If you take your early ballot directly to a polling location today in Maricopa County, you can present a valid ID to an election official to verify your identity and then, feed your early ballot into an on-site tabulator from 6am to 7pm. To find a list of acceptable ID’s, please visit [GetID.Maricopa.Vote](https://us.list-manage.com/yQUe1mEEKcU?e=a7ab36849c&c2id=b6e4918ecaa4a9e494d38fc9e6fde211) Those who participate in this option will have their vote included in election night results.Our state’s laws require all ballots to be received by 7:00 PM on Election Day to be counted.[**Maricopa County Voting Locations**](https://us.list-manage.com/kDHki7ENF4I?e=a7ab36849c&c2id=b6e4918ecaa4a9e494d38fc9e6fde211)[**Voting Locations Outside of Maricopa County**](https://us.list-manage.com/19d4D3NMTTM?e=a7ab36849c&c2id=b6e4918ecaa4a9e494d38fc9e6fde211)
I strongly encourage you to vote in person at the polls today and bring like-minded family and friends with you. The decisions made in this election will shape the future of Arizona, and that future belongs to the citizens who participate.Let's keep Arizona strong. Let's keep Arizona free. And let's make our voices heard.It has been an honor to serve this state. Best,**Shawnna**

YOUR IRA & 401(K) ISN'T ON THE BALLOT

Tomorrow you help pick who goes to (or stays in) Washington. One thing
isn't on your ballot: what your money buys.

Government figures out Thursday show prices rose half a percent in
September alone, and 3.6% over the past year.

When prices climb, the dollars in your savings buy a little less food,
a little less at the pharmacy, a little less of everything you live
on.

[Two grocery bags with prescription bottles on a kitchen table. A
label reading $100 in 2016 points to the left bag, full of bread,
apples, bananas and greens, with three pill bottles in front. A red
label reading Same $100 today: about $72 worth points to the right
bag, which holds much less, with two pill bottles. Caption: Your $100
from 2016 now buys about $72 worth.] [https://link.email.america1stwarroom.com/click/e9192142/UaHR0cHM6Ly9saW5rLmdvbGRjby5jb20vNTVwXQ/SZW1haWxfYW1lcmljYU9ORXN0d2Fycm9vbV9jb20yNjExMDM/LbmNsd0VCSTA1cg/gaunwdQ/s8p47e7fad8

Even Fed Chairman Kevin Warsh said last week that when Americans look
around,

_"...THEY SEE THE PRICES ARE UP."_
Fed Chairman Kevin Warsh

If you're retired, no boss hands you a raise to catch up. Your savings
just have to stretch further.

You can't vote on prices. But you can decide how your savings are
spread out [https://link.email.america1stwarroom.com/click/e9192142/UaHR0cHM6Ly9saW5rLmdvbGRjby5jb20vNTVwXS4/SZW1haWxfYW1lcmljYU9ORXN0d2Fycm9vbV9jb20yNjExMDM/LbmNsd0VCSTA1cg/gaunwdQ/sfja334b1e7

That's why savers near or in retirement can diversify part of their
savings into physical gold and silver.

From 1973 to 1979, when prices rose about 9% a year, gold rose about
35% a year. Silver soared too.

[Bar chart of average yearly rise from 1973 to 1979: prices rose
8.8% a year, gold rose 35% a year. Past performance is not a promise
of future results.] [https://link.email.america1stwarroom.com/click/e9192142/UaHR0cHM6Ly9saW5rLmdvbGRjby5jb20vNTVwXQ/SZW1haWxfYW1lcmljYU9ORXN0d2Fycm9vbV9jb20yNjExMDM/LbmNsd0VCSTA1cg/gaunwdQ/s8p47e7fad8

That's history, not a promise. Gold and silver have rough stretches
too, be very wary of anyone who says otherwise.

But through that long stretch of rising prices, gold and silver held
what money buys.

It comes from Goldco, which has helped Americans protect their

| **Your support has made a difference.**

Friend, Senator Maggie Hassan here. I had to take a moment to express my gratitude for your support. While we don’t know what will happen tonight or in the next coming days, I do know we wouldn’t have been able to support _Sherrod Brown_ in Ohio, _James Talarico_ in Texas,_Annie Andrews_ in South Carolina, _Mary Peltola_ in Alaska, or _Chris Pappas_ here in New Hampshire _(just to name a few!)_ without your generosity.

**Election Day is here, and if you haven’t voted already, I hope that you’re on your way to the polls.**

Thank you for being an important part of this coalition in Plymouth. I'm so grateful that I can count on you to help us fight for our democracy.

Families across the country are working hard to build better lives and achieve their version of the American Dream, and they need leaders — like the candidates we’ve supported all cycle — who will fight for them. We need to protect our freedoms, expand opportunities, and ensure that everyone has a fair shot at success.

_**Peggy Flanagan.**_
_**Deb Haaland.**_
_**Sharice Davids.**_
_**Claire Valdez.**_ It's Election Day. And by tonight, these five women are either in the history books or they're the reason we fight again. Today, Alaskans decide whether Mary Peltola flips the seat that decides the U.S. Senate. Minnesotans decide whether Peggy Flanagan becomes the first Native American woman EVER to serve in it — a first that has waited since 1789. New Mexicans decide whether Deb Haaland governs the state that barred her people from voting until 1948. Kansans and New Yorkers decide whether Sharice Davids and Claire Valdez hold the House's path to a majority. Everything that could be thrown at these five women has been thrown: $17 million, presidential rallies, a lawsuit, a demand that one of them not be allowed to run at all. This morning, every one of them is still standing — and the only voices left that matter belong to voters. So two asks today, in order: **First: vote.** If you live in Alaska, Minnesota, New Mexico, Kansas, or New York and haven't yet — go. Bring someone. **Second: fuel the final hours.** The Election Day operation is running right now — rides to the polls, final canvass shifts, every last supporter pulled across the line before polls close tonight. name: Brian Lenney
subject: Some people... lol
body:
ID Ed News just dropped a hard-hitting article this morning.

| |
---|---|---
|
# Some people... lol
| | | [Brian Lenney](https://substack.com/@brianlenney)
---
| Nov 3
---
| [](https://substack.com/@brianlenney)
---
ID Ed News just dropped a hard-hitting article this morning.

The guy who identifies as a reporter emailed me about my Pro-Tem announcement yesterday. Except, not really.

Because he went straight to asking me about some random X account's profile banner instead (because I DARED to retweet something they posted).

The something he got triggered over was this phrase: _**" some cultures are better than others." **_You know where I heard that argument originally? A black man, Thomas Sowell. So why did Sean the "reporter" try to paint me as racist for quoting a black man?
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/c6cf66c0-3909-478d-ad32-d45ccb507658?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---

Make it make sense Idaho Ed News!

Now, he could've asked me about anything. Like how Health and Welfare's books showed $433.6 million more cash than it actually had.

Or how the State Controller's office was off $102 million on revenue and $178 million on spending. Or why nobody was even checking those books against the Treasurer's books or the bank's.

Or the $72 million in IDHW grants that got sent to the AG for possible misuse, or illegal labor, or how PACs and lobbyists run the capitol, etc., etc.

But nay!

He didn't like me quoting a black man or the profile banner picture on some random X account's page and made the article about that.

(It's so 2021 of him, really)
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/9cee47c0-9ee7-4554-bb82-0a8381c5a2d2?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
So, why the weak article?

Here's why: the Idaho Big Ed lobby tells ID Ed News what to do, what to write, who to attack, what articles to pull down (they did this to me) and everyone knows it.

So my guess is they're still mad at how we rammed through [the bill to curbstomp the teachers unions](https://substack.com/@brianlenney/p-192690802) a few months ago and that's why they sent their attack dog after me.
Guess that means I'm over the target.
Cheers,
Brian
**P.S.** If you haven't already go vote today. If you're in Idaho [here's where you can find your sample ballot](https://substack.com/redirect/3eeceb28-dd97-484b-ae0d-d2eaee716140?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg). I like to print it off and fill it out before I walk into the polls.
**P.P.S.** If you haven't read Sowell on race and culture, here's the trilogy he wrote on it. A great place to start:
1. "Race and Culture: A World View"
2. "Migrations and Cultures"
3. "Conquests and Cultures"

(C) 2026 Brian Lenney

Election Day
| | | | | | [ ](https://ctrk.klclick.com/l/01M6GYB12NJK3M23Z3HERSAAR3_0)
---
| **Welcome to the Barlow for Wyoming Newsletter. Your hub for latest news, information and upcoming events.**
---
|
---
| | |
---
| **ALL IN**
---
| Hi Friends,Kelly and I have been talking about all the people we’ve met and the places we’ve been since August. It’s hard to believe we’re down to the last day of the campaign. We’re grateful, we’re excited, and we’re ready.You’ve welcomed us into your communities, shared meals with us, and stayed to visit long after an event was over. You’ve asked hard questions and trusted us with concerns about your families, your livelihoods, and your towns. We’ve learned a lot, and we’ll carry those conversations into the work ahead.There’s a lot of hope in Wyoming. We’ve heard it from young people wanting to build their lives here and from folks who have spent a lifetime making their communities better. People want to help. That gives Kelly and me a great deal of confidence in what we can accomplish together.First, let’s win this election.As I have said since day one, I am running for Wyoming, not against anyone. If you’ve already voted, thank you. If you haven’t, make today count for elections across our state, counties, and towns. Call your friends and check with your neighbors. We’ve worked too hard to take anything for granted. Let’s see it through.To our volunteers, staff, and advisors, thank you. You’ve given up evenings and weekends, put miles on your vehicles, and handled more details than anyone could count. Kelly and I know how much you’ve put into this.Most of all, thank you to the voters who got us here. We asked for your prayers, your money, and your votes. You kept showing up. You brought friends, put up signs, spoke on our behalf, and told us what you want for Wyoming. We’re proud to have earned your support, and we intend to honor it with our work.Please keep Wyoming in your prayers as we finish this election and, with your vote, take on the responsibility ahead. It means a great deal to have you with us.Let’s finish this, Wyoming. Then let’s get to work.Stay strong. Stay WyomingEric
---
| **ELECTION DAY MESSAGE FROM ERIC**
---
| | [ ](https://ctrk.klclick.com/l/01M6GYB12NJK3M23Z3HERSAAR3_1)
---
|
---
| ELECTION NIGHT VIDEO CALL
Join us TONIGHT from 7:30-8:00 pm for an election night message from Eric and Kelly, as well as other statewide Republican nominees!
---
| | |
1. Join by video via Google Meet by clicking [**here**](https://ctrk.klclick.com/l/01M6GYB12NJK3M23Z3HERSAAR3_2)
2. Dial in by phone at 323.741.1778 (Pin 676 690 620#)
3. Or, through this QR code->

---
| | |
---
| **WHAT'S NEXT?**
---
| **CAMPAIGN SIGN MANAGEMENT** As the campaign concludes, it is time to take down the Barlow for Governor signs. I appreciate each of you for putting them up and showing your support all this time. If you want to keep them, please do. The yard signs and thinner 4x4 and 4x8 signs will need to go into the garbage or could be used for sledding this winter! If you have one of the 4x4 or 4x8 thicker signs and it is in good shape, feel free to contact the campaign at scheduler@barlowforwyo.com, and we can make a plan to get them into storage for next time.
---
|
---
| **TRANSITION** If we are successful today, there will be an official transition website and office. Details will be available on the campaign website. My administration will need capable people who are ready to serve Wyoming.I will be looking for individuals who are respectful, listen and follow through. If you are interested in serving or know someone who is, please keep an eye out for the official website.
---
|
---
| **HEALTHCARE STRIKE TEAM** We're fast at work on healthcare solutions for Wyoming.Those who have signed up for the healthcare strike team effort will receive an email later this week about how to continue to help on Day One recommendations to share with Eric and the team.If you haven't signed up yet, please access the link below.

---
| | |
---
| **On The Trail**
---
| **GILLETTE** I joined student leaders from across Wyoming at Gillette College for the Wyoming Student Government Conference. We visited about leadership, serving our communities and helping others find their way.Student government gives young people a chance to listen to their peers, take on responsibility and work through disagreements. Those are skills our communities need, and I appreciate these students stepping up.Thank you to Student Senate President Josh Rogers and Gillette College for the invitation.
---
| | | | |
---
| | |
---
|
---
| **CHEYENNE** Appreciated the opportunity to meet with Tallgrass leadership and learn more about their operations across Wyoming, including new development south of Cheyenne. We also got a look inside their pipeline operations room. Always good to see firsthand the work happening across our state.
---
| | | | |
---
| | |
---
|
---
| | | **LARAMIE** One of the highlights of this campaign has been connecting with Wyoming students and young professionals who care about our state’s future.I enjoyed speaking at the ASUW Gubernatorial Forum in September and appreciated Ellu, a 19-year-old UW student, volunteering to share our message at the recent Albany County candidate forum hosted by ASUW, the UW Faculty Senate and UW Staff Senate.Over the past 14 months, we’ve heard from young people across Wyoming about their ideas, priorities and hopes for our state. Their enthusiasm and willingness to get involved have been encouraging.I’m grateful to everyone who has been part of those conversations. Wyoming’s future is bright!
---
| | |
---
|
---
| | | | |
---
| **CHEYENNE** Thanks to Boris, Mario and Noah with the Western States Regional Council of Carpenters. We talked about apprenticeships, partnerships with higher education and opportunities for young people to build careers in the trades. These are the folks helping build Wyoming’s economy, and I appreciate the work they do.
---
|
---
| **GILLETTE** Good morning from Gillette, where firefighters from across Wyoming are gathering for the Leadership 7220 conference! It was an honor to hear from folks who do so much to keep our communities safe. Thank you for your service and dedication to Wyoming.
---
| | | | |
---
| | |
---
|
---
| | | **CHEYENNE** Thanks to the Wyoming Taxpayers Association and Hank Halverson for inviting me to speak at its annual meeting in Cheyenne about Wyoming’s fiscal outlook.We had good discussions on road funding, legacy assets, workforce, data centers, tax policy and what’s ahead for the Legislature.These are smart, hardworking business owners who have a lot invested in Wyoming’s future. I appreciated hearing their questions and ideas.
---
| | |
---
| | | | |
---
| | |
---
|
---
| |
---
| | | | |
---
| **CHEYENNE** Good conversations with the Wyoming Rural Electric Association and electric cooperatives from across the state about keeping Wyoming powered today and into the future. Our co-ops play an important role in communities all across Wyoming, especially in our rural areas.

body:
Get Out to Vote.
Peter,
The day we’ve all been working so hard towards is finally here, and there’s only one final thing to say: **Get Out to Vote.**
Making your voice heard is an integral part of how our democracy works, and it would be a disservice to not include yours in one of the most important elections we’ve had.
This is your moment to remember how you felt these past 2 years:
All those moments where you drove past the gas station with wide eyes at how high the prices have gotten, and then still had to pull in because how else would your kids get to school the next day?
All those moments you felt unseen and unheard in spaces that should include you.
Those feelings are important.
Those memories are vital.
Because those are what get us to the polls today.
With Gratitude,
April McClain Delaney

| | | We finally made it, Team -- It's Election Day! We've spent a long two years watching opponents of voting rights run roughshod over our government and our democracy and now it's time for voters to let them know how we feel about it.

There's a lot on the line in today's elections, from the House and Senate to state legislatures, governors, Secretaries of State, and Attorneys General down to your local offices around the country. Voting rights and ballot access are 100% on the ballot, especially in the wake of extreme gerrymandering and the Supreme Court dismantling the VRA. Here's how you can get over the finish line:
---
* If you have not voted yet, **make sure you do your part and vote!**

* Once you're in line, no matter what, **stay in line**. Bring water, bring snacks, do everything you can to cast your ballot

**Tuesday, November 3, 2026**

Sprayer bottles are as well used as sponges in my household. I keep a few empty ones in storage because, as anyone who makes good use of sprayer bottles knows, the sprayer always breaks long before the bottle.
So I am left with a collection of plastic bottles without sprayers. I save them just in case, but just-in-case never comes.
Whenever I come across my stash, I wonder: Why do they not make sprayers that last as long as the bottles?
Before my frustration lasts longer than five seconds, however, I remind myself that it is not all about me. Or the hundreds of thousands of other people who, at some point today, will come across their own just-in-case stash of empty plastic bottles.

**Pause.
Breathe.
Look Deeper.

Refuel.**
**Welcome to Sweet Ground.**

Today, Nevada families get to decide what kind of state we want to live in. [_**If you haven’t voted yet, find your polling place and make a plan right now:**_](https://act.fordfornevada.com/go/240?t=3&akid=1264%2E127862%2E8ow_6g)

I know how close races get here. In 2018, I won my race for Attorney General by less than half a percent. Every vote mattered then, and every vote matters today.
So please, **go vote.** Bring your partner, your neighbor, your coworker. And if you’ve already voted, thank you. Help me get one more person to the polls today.
Thank you so much,
Aaron

Dear Friend,
Today is Election Day — the day that will decide who controls the House and the Senate, and with it the Congressional Majority.
This is the day we get to stand up for the values that made America the greatest nation on Earth - faith, family, freedom, and hard work. Every vote matters as we fight to secure the Congressional Majority and protect the country we cherish.
_Whether you’re at the polls right now casting your ballot, heading there in a few hours, or you’ve already voted up and down the ballot for our party, I wanted to take a moment on this critical day to thank you personally. Your support has meant more to me than I can say. Because of patriots like you, we are still standing strong and fighting for the America we love._
As a small token of my appreciation, I have a special Election Day surprise gift I would like to send directly to my supporters. **_[Please, confirm your address here:>](https://link.win.donaldjtrump.)_**
Please consider this my way of saying thank you for standing with me when our country needs it the most.
[CONFIRM ADDRESS](https://link.win.donaldjtrump.)
**_[I would also deeply appreciate it if you chipped in any amount: it can be SMALL or very GENEROUS — to help us finish strong today and deliver MASSIVE LANDSLIDE WINS to the Republican Party.>](https://link.win.donaldjtrump.)_**
With faith in God and love for this great country, we will continue the fight to protect the America we cherish.
**God bless you and your family,**
**And may God bless the United States of America.**
Sincerely,
Donald J. Trump

On January 12, 1865, twenty Black ministers sat down with General William T. Sherman at his Savannah headquarters -- men who had followed his army out of slavery and were camped by the tens of thousands along the Sea Islands. Asked what independence required, their spokesman, the Rev. Garrison Frazier, gave the record its cleanest sentence: "The way we can best take care of ourselves is to have land, and turn in and till it by our own labor." Four days later Sherman signed Special Field Order No. 15 -- the islands from Charleston south, the abandoned rice fields running thirty miles inland, the country along the St. Johns River on the Florida line. Roughly 400,000 acres, reserved for freed families in plots of not more than forty acres. Mostly Georgia's coast. Over the following months, some 40,000 freed people received possessory titles.
The mule never appears in the order; it arrived later, in soldiers' stories of animals handed to the families who worked them. And the titles were possessory -- Army-protected until Congress settled ownership. Still, the plan ran through Lincoln. In late March, at City Point, Sherman briefed him on the settlement and Lincoln lent his assent; historians argue over whether he ever meant outright deeds, but he raised no objection. By mid-April he was dead.

It's about the future of Wisconsin, the values we hold dear, and the kind of state we want to leave for our children and grandchildren. Tom Tiffany and I are running to bring common sense, affordability, and accountability back to Madison. That means fighting to end the 400-year property tax increase, lower utility bills, protect Wisconsin farmland from large-scale wind, solar, and data center developments, and keep men out of women's sports. We believe Wisconsin deserves leaders who will stand up for families in all 72 counties, listen to the communities they serve, and respect the values that make our communities strong. As conservatives, as Christians, and as Wisconsinites, it's important that we vote our values and make our voices heard. Please remind your family, friends, and neighbors that the polls are open and encourage them to vote for Tom Tiffany and David Varnam. Every vote matters. Thank you for your support and prayers throughout this journey. With your help, we can unlock Wisconsin's potential and build a future we can all be proud of. God bless, David Varnam

name: Dr. Shirley Weber
subject: Election Day Reminder: Go vote!
disclaimer_text: Paid for by Shirley Weber for Secretary of State 2026
body:
https://drshirleyweber.com/?utm_source=email%20wrapper&utm_medium=email%20wrapper&utm_campaign=email%20wrapper [https://drshirleyweber.com/?utm_source=email%20wrapper&utm_medium=email%20wrapper&utm_campaign=email%20wrapper]
Dear friends,

Today is Election Day, and I urge every eligible Californian to either return their ballot at a drop-box or find a polling place [https://www.sos.ca.gov/elections/polling-place] to vote in person.

As a child, Election Day was a special day for me. As a little girl, my mother opened our living room as a polling place – a reminder that democracy is not a spectator sport.

Today is Election Day. And your polling place is open. Exercise your right to vote, and cast your ballot.

You have a right to vote, even if you still need to register to vote or update your voter registration. If you’re unsure whether you’re registered to vote, or you’re not sure if you’ve updated your voter registration since you moved or changed your name, you can still conditionally register and vote at your polling place on Election Day [https://www.sos.ca.gov/elections/polling-place/] .

As Secretary of State, I’ve overseen voter registration drives and higher turnout than ever before. I’ve fought to protect poll workers from violent extremists. And I’ve been a transparent leader because trust is everything .

I want every eligible Californian to be able to vote whether or not I agree with you politically. And I’ll fight like hell to make sure that nothing stands between you and the ballot box .

Onward,

Dr. Shirley N. Weber

This is it, folks.
Everything we've worked towards comes down to today -- Election Day. Polls are officially open across Maine, and before I say anything else, I need to ask for your help:
**[Will you please give $15 right now to help me get every possible supporter to the polls and defeat Susan Collins? I launched a $150,000 Election Day turnout goal, and we don't have a minute to waste in hitting it.](https://substack.com/redirect/5e080c3b-bc7a-41c0-b9d2-37a610ea0d05?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)**
[HELP ME DEFEAT SUSAN COLLINS TODAY ->](https://substack.com/redirect/5e080c3b-bc7a-41c0-b9d2-37a610ea0d05?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
Look, I've spent a lot of my time in the Northern Woods of Maine as a logger. I learned that tough jobs aren't finished when you're tired - you keep pushing until you get the job done.
That's exactly how I view today.
My campaign has spent months traveling across the state, talking with Mainers about what matters most to them: lowering everyday costs, rooting out corruption, holding government officials accountable, and ending the pay-for-play scheme in Washington are some of the most common answers.
### **I can tell you confidently that Susan Collins represents the exact opposite.**
Still, poll after poll has shown me tied with Susan. We're running in the closest Senate race in the country, so we can't afford to kick our feet up on the final day and leave conversations unfinished with undecided voters.
That's why our campaign has mobilized a massive organizing team to knock on doors, make phone calls, and help voters get to the polls. We need to make sure they have the support and materials they need to get the job done.
Our team has spent down to $0, so our $150,000 voter turnout fund will do exactly that.
This is it, folks: Election Day is here, and I've never needed your help more than I do right now.
**[If you've been waiting for the perfect day to give, today is that day. Please give $15 (or more, if you can swing it) in the next hour to help us start Election Day strong and turn out every last Mainer to the polls.](https://substack.com/redirect/5e080c3b-bc7a-41c0-b9d2-37a610ea0d05?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)**
[GIVE $15: TURN OUT MAINE VOTERS ->](https://substack.com/redirect/5e080c3b-bc7a-41c0-b9d2-37a610ea0d05?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
I cannot begin to tell you how grateful I am for your support thus far. It's because of you that we have a real shot at defeating Susan Collins and flipping the Senate today.
Solidarity forever,
Troy

# **Somali community members describe fear, threats and violence for voicing criticism of Ilhan Omar**
Several sources **[told The NY Post](https://substack.com/redirect/7af1a315-4538-44ab-b574-7b9247de845e?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)** they've faced threats, online harassment, and in some cases physical assaults after speaking publicly about Rep. Ilhan Omar.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/7af1a315-4538-44ab-b574-7b9247de845e?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
* **One source described receiving a threatening phone call urging him to recant past statements** and instead publicly support Omar ahead of the midterms, while another said a man based in Somalia threatened to have him hospitalized over negative comments he made toward the congresswoman.
* **Another member of the Somali community who had spoken critically about Omar was assaulted in Minneapolis and again outside a restaurant in Kenya in 2022.** He said he was ambushed by a group of around 15 people and pepper-sprayed, then knocked to the ground and beaten -- left with a concussion. He believes a popular Somali TikTok influencer incited the attack claiming the influencer "set his followers" on him in retaliation for criticizing Omar.
* **The scrutiny stems partly from long-standing allegations that Omar 's 2009 marriage to Ahmed Nur Said Elmi,** reportedly her brother, was fraudulent for immigration purposes -- claims she has repeatedly denied.

# **Trump announces end to US military aid to Israel**
President Donald Trump said U.S. military and financial assistance to Israel, roughly $4 billion annually, **[will end at year's close,](https://substack.com/redirect/5ce1c5ce-3806-48d8-b7f3-cd7192f6ff7e?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)** explaining that Israel is thriving and no longer needs the support, which it can replace by purchasing weapons directly.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/5ce1c5ce-3806-48d8-b7f3-cd7192f6ff7e?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
* **Trump said Netanyahu himself proposed phasing out the aid after years of discussion,** framing the decision as mutual rather than one-sided, while noting Israel remains free to buy U.S. weapons going forward.
* **Trump acknowledged the political timing, tying the announcement to Michigan 's Senate race,** where Democrat Abdul El-Sayed has criticized Israel aid, while also linking the move to his broader push to reduce federal spending and balance the budget.
