Peter,

Most of what we send you is strategy: states, numbers, the plan to win. This one is about why we do this work at all. And that starts with Charlie Kirk.

Charlie launched Turning Point in the shadows of the Obama re-election campaign headquarters in Chicago. He was 18 years old.

Every established political force on the Left and the Right tried to stop him.

They failed.

What Charlie started grew into what is **the most influential activist organization in modern American history**.

We were privileged to work with him and be a part of this movement.

We joined Charlie because we believed our mission was the only viable way to save this country. Charlie was willing to do what nobody else in the conservative movement would do. He went looking for young Americans who cared enough about this country to act, and he gave them a reason to fight.

Then came 2020...

Under President Biden, we saw corruption, weaponization of the government, and a government promoting values that put Americans last.

Charlie was adamant that we do everything we could possibly do to fix this in 2024. **We DID IT** , and we must continue for 2026 and 2028 to have a shot at saving this country.

Now, it is on us to continue Charlie's vision and mission.

Every single day, we work to continue his legacy of recruiting, training, and mobilizing a new generation of citizens who love this country enough to do something about it.

That work does not stop at the campus gates. It's now changing the direction of the nation.

Right now, ballot chasers supported by Turning Point PAC are in the field in **states that will determine not just 2026, but the 2028 Presidential election**.

They are meeting voters face to face. They are building real relationships in these communities. They are chasing every ballot, whether it's cast on Election Day or by mail.

This is how we build the Red Wall.

Election Day is November 3rd.

subject: I'm speechless.
body:
# [](https://ginafortexas.com/?refcode=em_ms_gh_header)[](https://ginafortexas.com/?refcode=em_ms_gh_header)
Peter,
I didn’t expect to write you an email like this again. Not on Election Day.
If you’ve been waiting for the right moment to make your first gift to this campaign, this is it.
Here’s why I’m reaching out. A generous supporter has just offered to match grassroots donations up to $200,000 until polls close at 7 p.m. tonight, for one purpose: getting every last Texan who hasn’t voted to the polls.
_**That means if we raise $200,000, we’ll have $400,000 for our final get-out-the-vote push.**_ Every dollar you give becomes two.
As of today, more than 7.7 million Texans have already voted early, and the final polls show this race separated by a point or two. We feel good about what we’re seeing. But early votes only take us part of the way. **If we come up short today, everything we’ve built together over this campaign could be wasted.**
This race is going to come down to who shows up today. So every dollar of this match goes to the work that gets people there:
→ Gas money for the volunteers and staff driving across the state to reach voters
→ Walk lists, clipboards, and literature for canvassers knocking doors through tonight
→ Phone and text banks reminding voters where their polling place is and what they need to bring to the polls
→ Food and water to keep our volunteers going through long days
Greg Abbott has spent years and hundreds of millions of dollars trying to make sure Texans who are ready for change don’t show up today. This is how we fight back: door by door, call by call, text by text.
Here’s what one gift can do. Filling up a Texas-built Chevy Tahoe costs about $87.60. With the match, [**your $43.80**](https://act.ginafortexas.com/go/2683?c0=em_ms_gh_20261103_2_match.kftrd_&refcode=em20261103-2636&t=3&akid=2636%2E299639%2EDE9BG9) gift fills the whole tank for an organizer zig-zagging across town to reach voters.
[**Will you make your first gift now, while it’s doubled, to help us hit our $200,000 goal? Every dollar is matched until polls close tonight at 7 p.m., and it goes straight to turning out voters.**](https://act.ginafortexas.com/go/1356?c0=em_ms_gh_20261103_2_match.R3JFEZ&refcode=em20261103-2636&t=5&akid=2636%2E299639%2EDE9BG9)

[Give $250 (becomes $500!)](https://act.ginafortexas.com/go/2477?c0=em_ms_gh_20261103_2_match._TKQiS&refcode=em20261103-2636&t=10&akid=2636%2E299639%2EDE9BG9)
[Give another amount (all gifts 2X matched!)](https://act.ginafortexas.com/go/1356?c0=em_ms_gh_20261103_2_match.R3JFEZ&refcode=em20261103-2636&t=11&akid=2636%2E299639%2EDE9BG9)
Thank you. Let’s take Texas back.
Gina

My son and I woke up at 5 o'clock this morning, hit Dunkin', and delivered donuts to poll workers all across our neighborhood. It was a simple, humble way to kick off an Election Day where, to be perfectly honest, my nerves have been getting to me.
I'm nervous about what's going to happen today. I've heard a few folks toss around the term "nauseously optimistic," and I can't think of a better way to put it. The polls look good. The fundamentals look good. Our candidates are crushing it, our fundraising is up, and Fox News' ratings are down. It seems like Democrats are on the verge of a potentially historic midterm victory, thanks to Donald Trump's destruction of this country. And yet my stomach is in knots, because we know better than to take anything for granted.
I don't know what's going to happen today, and I won't pretend I do. There are going to be a lot of people giving you crap analysis of early vote numbers and today's turnout. Ignore them. My advice: keep your head down, do the work, go be with your family, keep your mental health in order, and be prepared for whatever comes next.
Because tonight, we will know. We'll know about the House, the Senate, the governor's races, and the state houses. By tomorrow morning, we'll most likely know the state of our union, and then we'll go from there, step by step.
* * *
**Today 's rant is sponsored by Ground News.**
And as the midterms wrap up, the flood of headlines, competing narratives, and political noise is only beginning. That's why I'll be using Ground News to cut through it all, to compare how the results are being covered, and get a clearer picture of what's actually happening.
Take this report--over 200 outlets picked up a story about President Trump threatening to ramp up vetoes in the case that Democrats win the House or Senate in the midterm elections.
**The Independent** says _If Republicans lose their majorities, Trump said he expects to issue vetoes for "a month or two" before negotiating agreements with opposition leaders._
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/e102acf9-bb0c-4215-8a9b-2d79d931e409?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
**New York Post** states _The president also agreed with[Elon Musk's recent warning](https://substack.com/redirect/b4ee3e50-6b9a-41d1-b0da-29349c17e333?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) that if Democrats sweep the elections on Tuesday, the country will be "maybe forever destroyed."_
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/e102acf9-bb0c-4215-8a9b-2d79d931e409?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
Same story--completely different narratives.

That's why I use Ground News. As we come to the head in this election cycle, it will be absolutely necessary to have the information I need to understand what is happening. 50,000+ sources aggregated from all over the world allow me to compare coverage side by side, see political bias, see whose money influences the narrative, to see how reliable they are and understand how framing changes the story about what's really going on in the election.

Being able to see how the left and right cover the same story, what each side emphasizes or leaves out, and discover overlooked stories with the Blindspot Feed, which surfaces coverage disproportionately reported by either side, will make understanding the outcome of the midterms even clearer.

I've been a paying user since before they ever sponsored Endless Urgency. I use it because it makes it a lot harder to be misled. They're completely subscriber funded so there are no corporate interests pushing a narrative on what you see.

See the full picture, instead of just one angle with Ground News. Subscribe through my link: **[https://groundnews.com/mikenellis](https://substack.com/redirect/e102acf9-bb0c-4215-8a9b-2d79d931e409?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)** for 40% off the same unlimited access Vantage Plan I use ->
[Subscribe](https://substack.com/redirect/9d49512c-fb17-4ab2-8a20-83118af88505?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
* * *
And if Donald Trump decides not to accept the results of this election, if they decide to cheat and steal (and I'm sure they're going to pull some shady shit today), we will fight back, and we will be prepared. As I told a lot of the election workers I met this morning: reach out to me if you need something, because I'm ready to get out there and fight. If ICE shows up at a polling location today, I'm going to be there, along with a lot of the other people who help organize my neighborhood. If a machine goes down (and I helped a guy fix one earlier this morning), we're going to be there bugging the county until it gets fixed.
That's what this looks like on the ground. It's not glamorous. It's donuts, broken machines, and making sure people know who to call if something goes sideways. But that's the work.
We're going to do this together, okay? Democracy takes a village, guys. A country takes a village. We've been holding each other together for so long, and that's exactly why I'm so grateful for this community.
Over this past year, this community, from Substack to YouTube to Threads and everywhere in between, has become something I value more than you could ever know. I hope I've been helpful to you, because I know you've been helpful to me. I might not be able to respond to every one of your comments, but I read most of them. I internalize them, and I use them to adjust, edit, and understand.
* * *
_I 've started paying more attention to how the same story can feel completely different depending on who's reporting it. Ground News makes that easy to see by showing coverage from across the political spectrum and pointing out what certain outlets leave out._
_My team and I use it because it helps cut through the noise._
**[See every side of every story with Ground News->](https://substack.com/redirect/9d49512c-fb17-4ab2-8a20-83118af88505?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)**
_Try it today!_
[ Subscribe](https://substack.com/redirect/9d49512c-fb17-4ab2-8a20-83118af88505?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
* * *
The conversation we're building together is key to taking our country back and building a better Democratic Party, one that can deliver for working people and fix what's broken in this country. And every time I'm out there doing cool shit, like roasting some conservative asshole on CNN, I get to do that because of you. I hope you know that.
So to everyone out there lifting up our democracy today, thank you. That means the poll workers doing thankless jobs, the campaign staff and volunteers knocking on doors, the folks who chipped in small-dollar contributions, and everyone who gave a little bit of themselves to whatever happens tonight. You're not just helping win elections. You're making sure our democracy survives and functions at a time when so many forces want to tear it down.
Whatever happens tonight, win, lose, or draw, you own a piece of it. Because when push came to shove, when Donald Trump and his MAGA movement came back into power, you said enough was enough. You didn't quit, and you didn't give up. You owned your part in this, and you were part of the solution in ways big and small, some we see and some we don't. A million acts of resistance. And you were one of those million acts more than a few times.
